text: The paper reports that debate and consultancy produce significantly different answer-transition patterns (chi2 = 19.81, p < 0.01); for mainstream-prior judges debate reduces correct-to-incorrect transitions (8.6% vs 22.9%, z = -4.21, p < 0.01) and preserves correct judgments more often (55.6% vs 40.5%, z = 3.23, p < 0.01), while skeptical-prior judges show similar patterns under both protocols (chi2 = 3.02, p = 0.39).
title: Debate reduces harmful correct-to-incorrect belief reversals for mainstream judges
